intro: American football is a game of territory played in short bursts. The attacking team (the offence) has four attempts — downs — to advance the ball ten yards; succeed and they earn four more. Every play stops and restarts from a line of scrimmage, turning each snap into a set piece planned in advance. This entry follows the NFL's rules; college and high-school football use their own rulebooks.
inThirtySeconds: Four downs to gain ten yards; reach it and the count resets.
Score a touchdown (6) by carrying or catching the ball in the end zone.
Each play starts from the line of scrimmage and ends when the ball carrier is down or a pass falls incomplete.
Fouls are punished by moving the ball backwards or forwards by a number of yards.
objective: Outscore the opponent with touchdowns, extra points, field goals and safeties over four quarters.

facts.players: 11 per team on the field; specialised offence, defence and special-teams units
facts.environment: Grass or artificial turf field with end zones and goalposts

scoring.label: Touchdown
scoring.detail: Possessing the ball in the opponent's end zone.

scoring.label: Extra point
scoring.detail: Kick through the uprights after a touchdown.

scoring.label: Two-point conversion
scoring.detail: Running or passing into the end zone again from close range after a touchdown.

scoring.label: Field goal
scoring.detail: Kick through the uprights during a normal play.

scoring.label: Safety
scoring.detail: The defence tackles the ball carrier in their own end zone, among other situations.

bodies.name: National Football League
bodies.scope: Professional league; publishes the NFL Rulebook

rulebooks.title: Official Playing Rules of the NFL

chapters.title: Downs and yards
chapters.summary: The system that structures every drive.

rules.title: Four downs to make ten yards
rules.summary: The offence has four plays (downs) to move the ball at least ten yards from where the series started.
rules.body: If they make it, they get a new 'first down' and four more tries. If they fail after four downs, the ball goes to the opponents at that spot — which is why teams usually punt or kick a field goal on fourth down rather than risk it.
rules.example: 'Third and 4' means it is the third attempt and 4 yards are still needed for a first down.

rules.title: The line of scrimmage
rules.summary: Every play starts with the ball on the ground at the line of scrimmage; the centre snaps it back to start the play.
rules.body: Before the snap, players must stay on their own side of the line. At least seven offensive players must line up on the line. A play ends when the ball carrier is down (a knee or body touches the ground after contact), goes out of bounds, scores, or a forward pass hits the ground.

chapters.title: Passing and catching
chapters.summary: One forward pass per play and what makes a catch.

rules.title: One forward pass per play
rules.summary: The offence may throw one forward pass per play, from behind the line of scrimmage.
rules.body: Backward passes (laterals) are allowed any time. An incomplete forward pass stops the clock and the play; the ball returns to the previous spot and a down is used.

rules.title: What is a catch
rules.summary: A receiver must gain control of the ball, get both feet (or another body part) down in bounds, and keep control long enough to make a football move.
rules.body: If the receiver loses the ball while going to the ground before completing the catch, it is incomplete. Catch rules have been revised several times; replay review is often used on close calls.

rules.title: Pass interference
rules.summary: Neither offensive nor defensive players may illegally hinder an opponent's chance to catch a forward pass once it is thrown.
rules.body: Defensive pass interference in the NFL is a spot foul: the offence gets a first down where the foul happened, which can mean dozens of yards.

rules.title: Kick-offs
rules.summary: Each half and every score (except some after a safety) is followed by a kick-off to the opponents.
rules.body: The NFL has substantially changed kick-off formations in recent seasons to reduce high-speed collisions; check the current rulebook for player alignment and touchback rules.

rules.title: Punts
rules.summary: On fourth down, the offence often punts the ball away to push the opponents back.
rules.body: The receiving team can return the punt or signal a fair catch to catch it without being tackled.

rules.title: Field goals
rules.summary: A kick from the ground (held by a teammate) that passes between the uprights and over the crossbar scores 3 points.
rules.body: A missed field goal gives the ball to the opponents at the spot of the kick (or the 20-yard line if further back).

chapters.title: Penalties
chapters.summary: Yards lost or gained for fouls.

rules.title: False start and offside
rules.summary: Moving before the snap (offence) or crossing the line of scrimmage early (defence) costs 5 yards.
rules.body: These are 'pre-snap' fouls: the play is usually stopped immediately or the foul enforced after the play.

rules.title: Holding
rules.summary: Grabbing or restricting an opponent who is not the ball carrier is holding.
rules.body: Offensive holding usually costs 10 yards; defensive holding gives 5 yards and an automatic first down.

rules.title: Personal fouls
rules.summary: Unnecessary roughness, roughing the passer and illegal hits to the head cost 15 yards.
rules.body: Player safety rules protect quarterbacks, receivers and kickers in defenceless positions. Flagrant fouls can also lead to ejection.

fouls.name: False start
fouls.description: Offensive player moves before the snap.

fouls.name: Defensive pass interference
fouls.description: Illegal contact with a receiver while the pass is in the air.
fouls.consequence: Ball placed at the foul spot, first down

fouls.name: Roughing the passer
fouls.description: Illegal hit on the quarterback after the throw.

fouls.name: Unnecessary roughness / flagrant hit
fouls.description: Dangerous contact, especially to the head.

flow.title: Coin toss and kick-off
flow.description: The toss decides who receives the opening kick-off.

flow.title: Drives
flow.description: The offence tries to string first downs together and score.

flow.title: Change of possession
flow.description: After a score, punt, turnover or failed fourth down, the other team attacks.

flow.title: Two-minute warning
flow.description: An automatic stoppage near the end of each half in the NFL.

flow.title: Overtime
flow.description: Tied games go to an overtime period with NFL possession rules.

positions.name: Quarterback
positions.role: Receives the snap and runs the offence, usually by passing.

positions.name: Running back
positions.role: Carries the ball on running plays and blocks.

positions.name: Wide receivers and tight end
positions.role: Catch passes; tight ends also block.

positions.name: Offensive line
positions.role: Five blockers protecting the quarterback and opening running lanes.

positions.name: Defensive line and linebackers
positions.role: Stop the run and pressure the quarterback.

positions.name: Cornerbacks and safeties
positions.role: Cover receivers and defend against passes.

positions.name: Kicker and punter
positions.role: Specialists for field goals, kick-offs and punts.

field.name: Field
field.dimensions: 120 yards × 53⅓ yards (100-yard field plus two 10-yard end zones)
notes: Yard lines every 5 yards, numbered every 10
Goalposts at the back of each end zone
Hash marks locate the ball between plays

glossary.definition: The centre passing the ball back to start a play.
Tackling the quarterback behind the line of scrimmage before a pass.
A defender catching a pass meant for the offence.
A ball carrier losing possession; either team can recover it.
The area inside the opponent's 20-yard line.

funFacts: The 'gridiron' nickname comes from the field's early markings, which formed a grid pattern.
Walter Camp introduced the line of scrimmage and the system of downs in the early 1880s.
